title: Noetherian regular rings are universally catenary
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then $R$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Explicitly, for every finite type commutative $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and every pair of primes $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$ of $A$, the lengths of finite strict prime chains between them are bounded by a finite integer, and all saturated chains between them have the same length. A chain is saturated if no prime can be inserted strictly between successive members, and its length is the number of strict inclusions. No finite bound on the dimensions of all local rings of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary, regular-ring consequence using Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM. The hypotheses are Noetherianity and regularity at every prime; the conclusion is universal catenarity, not merely catenarity of R.

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq R$ and put $S=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $d=\dim S$. By hypothesis $S$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: it is Noetherian local and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $d$ elements $x_1,\dots,x_d$ ($d$ is finite since $S$ is Noetherian local). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is an $S$-regular sequence in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; since $\mathfrak mS
eq S$, the definition of depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge d$. Conversely $S
eq0$ is a finite $S$-module with $S_{\mathfrak q}
eq0$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, so $\operatorname{Supp}(S)=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(S)=\dim S=d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)\le d$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})=\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$, the local Cohen–Macaulay condition required by the next step. For $d=0$ the sequence is empty ($S$ is a field) and both inequalities read $0$; no uniform bound on the dimensions of the localizations is used.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM, last sentence 'In particular R is Cohen-Macaulay') applied at each localization R_p, with the bound depth <= dim of Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cm-ring-universally-catenary] to the Noetherian ring $R$ and the local Cohen–Macaulay conclusions of Step 1. It yields universal catenarity in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Unfolding that definition gives, for every finite type $R$-algebra $A$ and every comparable pair of primes $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak b$, a finite bound on lengths of strict prime chains and equality of lengths for all saturated chains, exactly the explicit conclusion stated here.
